items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1878

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the economic development law, in relation to including
the name of the individual or business enterprise that has been awarded
an identical or substantially similar procurement contract in certain
notices of procurement contract opportunities

 
PURPOSE:

Require disclosure of an incumbent of a procurement contract in the
procurement opportunities newsletter published by the Commissioner of
Economic Development.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends section 142 of economic development law to require
disclosure of the name of any individual or business enterprise that has
been awarded an identical or substantially similar procurement contract
within the pat five years.

Section 2: Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under current law, there is no requirement of the Commissioner to
include the identity of the incumbent of a procurement contract in the
procurement opportunities newsletter. This bill would increase transpar-
ency in the procurement process by providing information on the current
vendor.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020 - S8213A Referred to Commerce, Economic Development And Small Busi-
ness - Print Number 8213A / No Assembly Same-as

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1878B

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the economic development law, in relation to including
the name of the individual or business enterprise that has been awarded
an identical or substantially similar procurement contract in certain
notices of procurement contract opportunities

 
PURPOSE OF THE BILL:

This bill require the disclosure of an incumbent of a procurement
contract in the procurement opportunities newsletter published by the
Commissioner of Economic Development.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the.bill amends section 142 of Economic Development Law
to require disclosure of the name of the individual or business that was
awarded an identical or substantially similar procurement contract with-
in the past five years.

Section two relates to the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

Clarified that the contracting agency must disclose the identity of an
identical or substantially similar contract.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under current law, there is no requirement for the contracting agency to
disclose the identity of an incumbent of a contract in the procurement
opportunities newsletter. This bill would increase transparency in the
procurement process by providing information on the current vendor.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

A10432 of 2020.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
